candidates.label: the reference's missing modes, real beating
candidates.hypothesis: The listener heard 'a simple clean tone' where the reference is 'a resonant wavy metallic ring', and two bound axes say the same thing: mode density 1.107 vs 1.898 (0.58x -- the 'too plain' end of the metallic-complexity question) and beating depth 0.490 vs 0.611 ('too steady'). Reading the reference's own mode ratios out of the descriptor (12 modes at 0, 846, 1509, 1768, 2048, 2498, 2882, 2973, 3215, 3505, 3678, 4178 cents above its 574 Hz anchor) against the synth's (only the first 7: 0, 831, 1495, 1757, 2037, 2490, 2874) shows exactly what is missing: the synth reproduces the reference's lower seven modes to within ~15 cents and has NO partner for its top five. So the mean 271-cent 'mode ratios' gap is not mistuning, it is absence. Slots gen9-gen12 are unused, so the four lowest missing modes go in at the reference's measured ratios -- 2973/3215/3505/3678 cents = 3.4527/3.9711/4.6961/5.1880 x the voice fundamental, each with its own env_fast_rate so it decays independently: mode density 1.107 -> 1.582 (gap to the reference -60%). For the waviness, gen3 is the gen2 beat partner; moving it 1.005 -> 1.0040 halves the beat interval and beating depth reads 0.620 vs 0.611 (drift -> ok, gap -92%), with lfo_enabled 0 so the wobble is REAL partial beating rather than a 3.2 Hz tremolo layered on top. Nothing here touches amp_decay/amp_release or gen1_freq: ring T60 stays ok at 2.98 s vs 2.97 s and mode anchor stays ok at 577 Hz vs 574 Hz. The PREDICTIVE axis improves too -- inharmonicity 0.00398 -> 0.00450 against the reference's 0.00928 -- because the added modes are inharmonic. band T60 and onset bite remain the two bound drifts.

candidates.label: per-mode decay: the hum outlives the strike
candidates.hypothesis: A structurally different route to the same 'resonant wavy ring': leave the mode bank and the LFO alone and reshape WHICH modes last. The reference's decay-per-mode vector is -1.9, -3.4, -5.8, -63.8, -13.6, -23.7, -50.4, -43.3 dB/s -- a 33x spread in which the hum outlives everything and the upper modes die fast. The synth's is -4.6, -5.2, -5.3, -5.7, -6.2, -6.9 dB/s: every mode decaying at the same rate because the shared amp envelope dominates, which is precisely why it reads as one flat 'clean tone'. gen1_env_fast_rate 0.03 -> 0 lets the hum ride the amp envelope alone (the reference's slowest mode), and gen8_env_fast_rate 0.30 -> 5.30 puts the top mode on the reference's own -50 dB/s. That alone takes band T60 from drift (mean 2.43x long, worst 4k 6.52x) to ok (mean 1.51x, worst 500 2.06x). It does NOT help the strike: onset bite goes 660.6 -> 2635.7 against the reference's 29.4 (89.78x, drift before and after, and further away) -- the shorter upper modes leave less energy in the 300-600 ms window the ratio divides by, so the clank reads louder. That is the row to listen to on this candidate. gen3_freq 1.005 -> 1.0040 is shared with A -- it is the only lever measured to move beating depth toward the reference (0.490 -> 0.624, drift -> ok) -- but everything else differs: A adds four partials and removes the LFO, B adds none and keeps it. Deliberately NOT changed: amp_decay/amp_release (ring T60 stays ok, 2.98 s vs 2.97 s -- the listener asked for a ring that PROLONGS) and gen1_freq (mode anchor stays ok at 577 Hz). Only gen6/gen7 were left at their seed rates: speeding them to the reference's -13.6/-23.7 dB/s strips enough upper partial energy to drag inharmonicity from 0.0040 to 0.0029, away from the reference's 0.0093, and `refs validate` scores inharmonicity AUC 1.00 against the ear verdicts. Bound drift left: onset bite only.

candidates.label: reed chiff instead of a breath bed
candidates.hypothesis: The listener's words are 'way too airy/breathy, needs warmness', and the cause is structural: the reed-buzz slot gen1 runs env_tail_mix 0.6 at env_tail_rate 0.0 -- a CONSTANT noise bed that never decays -- which is exactly what noise persistence measures (late-half noise / early-half noise) and why it reads 0.860 against the reference's 0.338. Zeroing gen1_env_tail_mix and turning the slot into a decaying chiff (env_fast_mix 0.6 -> 1.5, env_fast_rate 10 -> 4) gives a breath that BLOWS and then goes, like a tongued reed: noise persistence 0.860 -> 0.422, closing 84% of the gap. That edit alone overshoots the warmth -- brightness ratio falls 7.73 -> 5.93, past the reference's 6.92 and further from it than the current version -- so filter_cutoff 7000 -> 9000 lets the upper reed formant back through and lands 6.62, closing 64% of the brightness gap from the correct side. amp_release 0.10 -> 0.13 settles modulation flatness at 0.689 vs the reference's 0.687 (drift -> ok), which is the 'steadiness' question's axis. amp_attack stays at its shipped 0.012 s: a tongued oboe speaks in tens of milliseconds, and the reference's 1.14 s attack is that PERFORMANCE's swell, not the instrument (env.attack is a recorded gate exemption for this family). Every bound axis lands ok, and the PREDICTIVE axis improves: inharmonicity 0.00594 -> 0.00326 against the reference's 0.00038.

candidates.label: formant bank on the nasal peak
candidates.hypothesis: A's noise fix and amp_release, then a structurally different answer to the warmth: no filter change at all, and instead the FORMANT stage plus a reed-shaped harmonic bank. first formant reads 2449 Hz against the reference's 1472 Hz (+66%) -- the additive bank has no resonance there -- so formant_enabled 1 with vowel 'a' on voice_type 1 and formant_shift 1.2 places the bank's first formant at 1521 Hz, +3% of the reference. formant_mix is held at 0.35, under the 0.5 the guide warns about: above it a fixed formant bank vocodes the source and the oboe starts reading as a sung vowel rather than a reed. The brightness comes back not by opening a filter but by THINNING the fundamental -- gen2_gain (H1) 0.42 -> 0.24 and gen3_gain (H2) 0.12 -> 0.08 -- which is the real oboe's own spectrum (a weak H1 under an H3 peak, the measured reference reads H1 1.0 / H2 0.26 / H3 1.39): brightness ratio 7.73 -> 6.16 vs the reference's 6.92, a 7% closer gap. It also sharpens the breath fix: noise persistence 0.860 -> 0.374, closing 93% of the gap, because there is less fundamental for the residual to hide under. modulation flatness 0.689 (ok), inharmonicity 0.00594 -> 0.00326 (PREDICTIVE, improved).
